title: Deformation response and energy evolution of slotted coal subjected to cyclic loading
content:
by Xiaoyan Sun, Ke Xu, Haolong Zheng, Hao Liu, Han Liu, Tengfei Ma

Given the challenges posed by low gas permeability and complex hydraulic fracturing disturbance environments in deep low-permeability reservoirs, this study conducted cyclic loading and unloading tests with different cyclic amplitudes and fracture angles to investigate the deformation response and energy evolution of slotted coal under the effects of external disturbances and fracture angles. The results indicate that the peak strength and peak strain of the coal specimens decrease with increasing fracture angle, while the peak strain increases with increasing cyclic amplitude. During the low-stress loading phase, the modulus of the coal specimens first increase and then gradually stabilize. As failure approaches, plastic deformation accumulates rapidly, and the modulus during loading and unloading decreases sharply. The coal specimens’ resistance to deformation is negatively correlated with the loading amplitude and fracture angle. As the fracture angle increases, the failure mode of the coal specimens changes from “shear failure dominant” to “tensile-shear mixed failure” to “tensile failure dominant.” Increasing cyclic amplitude enhances the damage caused by a single cycle to the specimen, exacerbating the cyclic effects of fatigue deformation and internal damage within the coal specimen, leading to greater energy dissipation and the formation of more microfractures and fractured structures. Fracture angles of 36° and 45° may be more conducive to the development and connectivity of coal seam fractures. The research findings provide reasonable theoretical guidance for methane extraction in low-permeability reservoirs, holding significant scientific and engineering value.
author: Xiaoyan Sun
